perspective:
From my perspective as Bradley Ochoa:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager.
- Katherine and I have a professional relationship that can be strained because we disagree about sales and marketing strategy.
- I prepared data and charts to support traditional sales techniques, which I believe are proven but being overlooked in favor of the newer digital strategies Katherine supports.
- In our meeting room, I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional methods would benefit core sales more, and I showed her data from our last five campaigns.
- I heard Katherine say the market is evolving, that we cannot ignore digital outreach, and she asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement.
- I replied that I was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but was frustrated that proven methods felt sidelined without proper consideration.
- I heard Katherine say she understood my frustration, that it is about balance, and that we should analyze the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales.
- I asked Katherine to explain how those digital strategies are developed.
- Katherine told me it is about targeting the right audience with the right message, and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind the campaign.
- I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing those outcomes made me want to understand the digital approach more.
- Katherine said she was glad I was open to exploring it, that adapting and evolving with market trends is important, and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I began to question my staunch support for only traditional methods.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting, saying a combined approach could strengthen our campaigns.
- Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results and that we should schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps.
- I said I was hopeful that leveraging both our expertise could create something impactful, and I appreciated her willingness to collaborate.
- Katherine said she looked forward to it and that it was about leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After our successful joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas.
- I showed Katherine the draft and said I was excited about its potential.
- Katherine reviewed it and said it looked comprehensive, well thought out, and that my hard work showed.
- I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors, and that I wanted to make sure we nailed the presentation.
- Katherine said she was confident we would, and suggested going through it once more to fine-tune areas that needed it.
- After the presentation succeeded and the new strategy was implemented, I thanked Katherine, said I learned a lot from her, and felt grateful for my professional growth through our collaboration.
- Katherine said it had been a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition, and that my openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership.
- I proposed regular strategy sessions to continue our collaboration.
- Katherine said that was a fantastic idea and would keep us on top of our game and market trends.
- I only have access to my own thoughts, feelings, actions, and what Katherine said or did in our interactions. I do not have access to her private thoughts, personality type, education, or any hidden/narrator-only information.
